issues.legal_issue: A testamentary claimant need not obtain probate to establish rights under a will when the will and the relevant immovable property fall outside the territorial categories covered by the probate requirement.
material_facts: The dispute concerned a self-acquired immovable property in Delhi bequeathed by will and codicil to both sides.
The respondents brought a civil suit seeking declarations and an injunction concerning the will and codicil, while the appellant brought a suit asserting succession by law.
The Single Judge rejected the respondents’ plaint on the ground that probate was required; the High Court’s Division Bench set that order aside.
issues.conclusion: Probate or letters of administration were not required for the wills concerning the property in this case. The High Court’s Division Bench was correct, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 213(1) read with Section 213(2) and Section 57(a) and (b) of the Indian Succession Act, the probate requirement applies to wills of Hindus, Buddhists, Sikhs and Jains only when they fall within the territorial categories in Section 57(a) or (b). Section 57(c) does not attract Section 213 because Section 213(2) refers only to the classes specified in clauses (a) and (b). The Court’s interpretation was supported by Ram Chand v. Sardara Singh, M/s. Behari Lal Ram Charan v. Karam Chand Sahni, Winifred Nora Theophilus v. Lila Deane, Rajan Suri v. State, and Clarence Pais v. Union of India.

predicates.civil_claim_seeks_right_under_will: A claimant brings a civil proceeding to establish a legal entitlement by relying on a will.
predicates.testator_belongs_to_covered_religious_cl: The person who made the will belonged to one of the religious communities to which this rule applies.
predicates.will_made_outside_designated_territories: The will was made outside the territories in which the relevant territorial category applies.
predicates.immovable_property_outside_designated_te: The immovable property to which the claim relates is situated outside those territories.
predicates.probate_not_required_to_establish_right_: A claimant may establish the claimed right under the will without first obtaining probate or letters of administration.

issues.definition: When a civil claimant relies on a will made by a person in the covered religious class, and both the will and the relevant immovable property are outside the designated territories, probate is not required to establish the claimed right.
